paragraphs.text: A home weather station usually consists of an outdoor sensor unit and an indoor display. The sensors are mounted on a pole at least two metres above the ground, away from walls that could store heat.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: At the top of the unit, three small cups called an anemometer spin in the wind; the faster they turn, the higher the wind speed. Beside them, a vane points in the direction the wind is coming from.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Rain falls into a funnel and fills a tiny bucket that tips over each time it collects a set amount, sending a signal to the display. Temperature and humidity are measured inside a white shield with slatted sides, which protects the sensors from direct sunlight.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: The indoor display receives the data by radio and can store a year of readings.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Many home weather stations can also share their readings online, where they help to build detailed maps of local weather conditions.
paragraphs.label: E
